issue.title: fix: enforce remote sandbox refusal for discovery and skill reads

repository.name: CorbanuTerminal
repository.description: Corbanu Terminal: a capital-markets-focused AI coding and agent terminal.

issue.body:
Refs #2088; follows #2087 (D510/D491).

Moderate and Aggressive now carry the existing sandbox refusal through executor skill/plugin discovery and resource reads, including full-disk profiles and catalogs captured before a live security-level change. Remote discovery checks the executor before sending roots, and the receiving executor rechecks elevated sandbox setup for marked file operations. Ready remote environments without a usable sandbox receive a startup notice with setup steps. Permissive behavior and the wire schema are unchanged.

This is a bounded repair of D491/D510. Product citation: **Reconciled security scope — TO BUILD**, “preserves Permissive compatibility and makes the broker mandatory for both Moderate and Aggressive.” Release-note fragment and sandbox documentation included.

Validation on glitch, Rust 1.99.1, isolated test homes and target:
- Four regressions fail on unchanged main: discovery precheck, full-disk context, live skill-read context, and startup notice. All pass after the fix using the existing harness/fake executor.
- Focused exec-server tests: 6 passed. Full skills-extension suite: 72 passed. Focused core tests: 68 passed. Integration regressions (#1976/#2000/#2050/#2167, including the #2088 startup assertions): 20 passed. Developer-accounting #2088 regression: 1 passed.
- `just fix` made no changes; clippy including tests with `-D warnings` passed. Matching local worktree `just fmt`, diff checks, and release-fragment validation passed.
- An initial pass-after run reused a stale baseline skills library because archive synchronization preserved old timestamps. Refreshed changed-source timestamps and reran fix, clippy and all listed tests successfully. No tests were removed. Native Windows elevated-not-set-up fail-before and a real Windows remote executor/TUI exercise were not run locally. Native Windows CI, including clippy, tests, integration, security probes, and credential canaries, passed.

Native Windows clippy exposed a Send-proof recursion overflow through the new startup await. Boxing that future bounds the compiler's type proof without changing behavior or tests. Core fix/clippy, 68 focused tests, 20 integration tests, and developer-accounting all pass again on the revised head.

Independent read-only Opus 5.5 High review round 3: **APPROVE** on `16ff8474665e292f84305be2c18c58c678b73008` (3/5 rounds). Matching corbanu-security approval posted after that verdict. All 42 applicable CI checks passed (10 workflow skips, no failures or pending checks). SAME-TEST, clean merged-tree/blob-size, exact-head approval, and literal-head merge guards passed. Merged as `66da17e93cff18fde7ca412e7a500f9747c50d70`.

Compatibility limits: protected discovery requires the existing discoverV1 capability (introduced before hostSandbox reporting); older executors need updating. Startup notices cover connections ready at startup and check them sequentially; deferred connections explain refusal on first use.

Remaining #2088 decisions for Travis:
- Items 1/6: add a negotiated launch requirement and actual per-process confinement provenance, or retain client prechecks. Recommend a separately signed-off, backward-compatible protocol design preserving unmarked Permissive launches. The existing-field file-operation case is fixed here.
- Item 3: correct PF-27-S06's target-platform check across all levels, or restrict it to protected modes. Recommend the complete correction after explicit security sign-off because it also changes post-taint Permissive behavior.
- Item 5: cache positive sandbox reports by URL, or keep fresh checks until executor identity/invalidation is specified. Recommend fresh checks; a time-only cache weakens refusal after an executor swap or setup change.

body:
Merged #2257 to main as `66da17e93cff18fde7ca412e7a500f9747c50d70` (reviewed head `16ff8474665e292f84305be2c18c58c678b73008`). This ships the D491/D510-compatible portion of this issue.

- Item 1 (file operations): receiving Windows executors recheck elevated setup on requests carrying the existing refusal, including full-disk operations that do not invoke the helper.
- Item 2: protected-level refusal now reaches skill/plugin capability-root discovery and skill resource reads, including full-disk profiles and locally under D491. The read path keeps the live refusal when the catalog was captured without a sandbox context.
- Item 4: ready remote environments without a usable sandbox get a startup notice with setup/upgrade steps; the session still starts. Deferred connections retain first-use refusal.

Four regression cases failed before and pass after using the existing harness/fake executor. Glitch Rust 1.99.1 clippy and focused tests passed (6 exec-server, 72 skills, 68 core, 20 integration, 1 developer-accounting). Exact-head independent Opus 5.5 High review round 3 APPROVED, followed by matching corbanu-security approval. All 42 applicable CI checks passed, including Windows clippy, native tests, integration, security probes, and credential canaries; no pending checks at merge. The PR has the complete validation record and release fragment. Native Windows fail-before and a real remote Windows/TUI exercise were not run locally.

Keeping this issue open for Travis's remaining decisions:
1. Items 1 (command launches) and 6: use a negotiated launch marker and actual per-process confinement provenance, or retain client prechecks. Recommendation: a separately signed-off, backward-compatible protocol design preserving unmarked Permissive launches. Other clients depend on this wire protocol.
2. Item 3 (PF-27-S06): correct executor-platform handling across all levels, or limit a repair to protected modes. Recommendation: complete target-platform correction after explicit security sign-off, because the full correction changes post-taint Permissive behavior beyond D491/D510.
3. Item 5: cache positive sandbox reports by URL, or keep fresh checks until executor identity and invalidation are specified. Recommendation: keep fresh checks; a time-only cache can fail open after an executor swap or setup change.

No protocol change or additional Permissive restriction is included in #2257. Protected discovery uses the existing discoverV1 capability, so older executors lacking it need updating. Startup checks are sequential; readiness-event notifications can be a later follow-up.

issue.title: Upstream Codex sync to rust-v0.165.0: scoping report

repository.name: CorbanuTerminal
repository.description: Corbanu Terminal: a capital-markets-focused AI coding and agent terminal.

issue.body:
This report measures what a fresh merge of upstream OpenAI Codex into `main` would take. It makes no decisions. The starting point is #94 by @goodalexander, who merged upstream `rust-v0.147.0` into the fork and wrote the upgrade record. That PR mapped the hotspots and the retained-behaviour checklist this sync needs, so thank you. #94 is being closed in favour of this sync (owner decision D219).

## Target and baseline

| | |
|---|---|
| Newest stable upstream release | `rust-v0.165.0` (published 2026-10-27), commit `360319d8dee62d87e2d59fc0c21805d79519cfed` |
| `main` measured at | `70281fe4e76d3a75ea52f406946b2224364d97b0` (2026-10-29) |
| Merge base (`main` ∩ 0.165.0) | `413492cd6c3a4d4f8dff6f406247ccda5a9d88aa` (2026-07-30), the same base #94 started from |
| Upstream commits since base | **3,807** (3,616 of them came after 0.147.0) |
| `main` commits since base | **6,731** |
| Upstream diff since base | 7,847 files, +1.19M / −208k lines |
| Toolchain | Rust 1.99.1 on both sides (no bump). `v8` goes 150.4.0 → **152.2.0** |

## Trial merge result

`git merge --no-commit --no-ff rust-v0.165.0` in a throwaway worktree on a local-only branch, aborted afterwards:

- **873 conflicted files**: 773 content, 62 modify/delete, 32 file-location (upstream directory moves), 6 add/add.
- **2,885 conflict hunks**, about **134k lines** inside conflict markers.
- 326 of the 873 are test files, including 135 insta snapshots. 38 are generated schemas or lockfiles that get regenerated, not hand-merged.
- For comparison: merging #94's target (0.147.0) into today's `main` gives 138 conflicts. On 2026-09-06 it gave 44. The gap grows quickly as both sides move.

### By area

| Area | Files | Hunks | Lines in conflict | Notes |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---|
| tui | 259 | 621 | 33.5k | 20 modify/delete, 24 moved (`tui/src/analytics`) |
| core | 211 | 955 | 47.0k | 16 modify/delete (shell handlers, remote compaction) |
| other crates/tooling | 161 | 370 | 11.6k | state, ext, rollout, cli, mcp-server, core-skills, scripts |
| app-server | 56 | 195 | 8.3k | |
| config / providers / auth | 45 | 177 | 7.4k | model-provider(-info), models-manager, login |
| sandboxing (linux, network-proxy, shell-escalation) | 38 | 144 | 11.1k | `bwrap.rs` alone has 3.9k lines in conflict |
| config/schemas/locks | 38 | 241 | 7.7k | regenerate (`Cargo.lock`, `MODULE.bazel.lock`, schemas, `models.json`) |
| windows-sandbox | 20 | 61 | 3.3k | |
| CI/workflows | 16 | 44 | 1.0k | 4 workflows/actions deleted upstream |
| protocol (+ app-server-protocol src) | 15 | 40 | 1.8k | |
| exec / exec-server | 14 | 37 | 1.1k | |

### Heaviest hotspots

| File | Hunks | Lines | Corbanu features touched |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| `core/src/session/mod.rs` | 60 | 2,458 | session wiring (security/provenance, accounting, agents) |
| `core/src/client.rs` | 45 | 2,315 | providers/catalog, permissions classifier hooks |
| `tui/src/app/tests.rs` | 18 | 9,067 | agents, vault, branding, classifier |
| `models-manager/models.json` | 37 | 4,423 | provider catalog, branding (regenerate + re-apply) |
| `linux-sandbox/src/bwrap.rs` | 23 | 3,865 | sandbox boundary |
| `tui/src/lib.rs` | 25 | 2,951 | branding/home dir, startup |
| `tui/src/app_server_session.rs` | 35 | 1,065 | session/agents |
| `core/src/session/turn.rs` | 34 | 723 | turn loop (classifier, agents) |
| `login/src/auth/manager.rs` | 27 | 971 | vault-backed credentials, providers |
| `network-proxy/src/credential_broker.rs` | 15 | 1,914 | credentials / sandbox network |
| `tui/src/model_catalog.rs` | 3 | 381 | provider catalog (346 Corbanu catalog lines on our side) |
| `core/src/agent/control.rs` + `control/mailbox.rs` | 18 | 1,454 | spawn / agent graph / mailbox |
| `tui/src/chatwidget/slash_dispatch.rs` | 7 | 352 | `/tasknode`, `/vault`, wallet/GPU slash commands |
| `core/src/exec_policy.rs` (+tests) | 8 | 772 | permissions classifier, vault, branding |

How often Corbanu identifiers show up on our side of the conflict hunks (approximate keyword match): branding/home dir 152 files, sandbox 119, spawn/agents 43 (agent-specific terms), providers/catalog 64, vault 39, permissions classifier 38, wallet/GPU/plan 29, Task Node 10. The classifier itself (`core/src/security/`) and the Corbanu-only crates (vault, tasknode-session, wallet, telegram) **do not conflict**. What conflicts is the upstream code that calls them.

### Structural upstream changes (these need porting, not just conflict resolution)

- **Shell tools moved onto unified exec** (upstream #39757). Upstream deleted `core/src/tools/handlers/shell.rs`, `runtimes/shell.rs` and `unix_escalation.rs`. `main` has 38 commits on those files. Our permission/sandbox behaviour there has to be re-hosted on the unified-exec path. **This is the main security risk.**
- **Patched zsh backend removed** (`shell-escalation` crate, #52160). **`codex mcp-server` removed** (#42993). **Legacy remote compaction removed** (#44273). `core-skills/src` split across several crates.
- **Repo guidance removed upstream** (`AGENTS.md`, `.codex/skills`, #49713). Keep ours.
- **24 new upstream crates**, some of which overlap with Corbanu features: `agent-roles`, `message-board`, `runtime-agent-instance` (vs our agent graph/mailbox), `mxc-sandbox`, `windows-sandbox-service`, `user-verification`, `workload-identity`, `guardian-context`.

## Effort and risk (rough)

- **Effort:** about 3–5 weeks of focused integrator work plus reviews, for one owner with agent help. Roughly 1–1.5 weeks for core + session, 1 week for tui, 1 week for sandbox/permissions porting and security review, and the rest for app-server/protocol/config, regeneration, CI and Windows.
- **Risk: high.** It changes the sandbox and permission surface (unified exec port, bwrap, windows sandbox, network-proxy credentials), so it needs security sign-off. The TUI conflicts are wide and snapshot-heavy. `main` is very active (about 70 commits/day since July), so a long-lived branch will drift. Each week of delay adds conflicts (0.147.0: 44 → 138 conflicts in 7 weeks).

## Suggested staging plan

1. **Freeze the target** at `rust-v0.165.0` and don't chase newer releases mid-sync. Keep one integration branch with a real two-parent merge, as #94 did.
2. **Mechanical pass:** take upstream for deleted/moved files where `main` didn't diverge meaningfully, keep our `AGENTS.md`/skills, regenerate lockfiles, `models.json` (then re-apply the Corbanu catalog), app-server and config schemas, and re-accept snapshots last.
3. **Per-area slices, one commit and one review each:** protocol/app-server-protocol → config/providers/auth (catalog, vault-backed login) → core (session, client, turn, agents/mailbox) → exec/unified-exec → tui (branding/home dir, catalog popups, slash commands, Task Node, `/spawn`) → app-server → other crates.
4. **Security slice (stops at "needs security sign-off"):** port the shell-handler permission/classifier/sandbox behaviour onto unified exec, plus bwrap, windows-sandbox, network-proxy `credential_broker` and `exec_policy`. Fail-before/pass-after tests for every boundary that moved.
5. **Qualification:** full CI including Windows clippy and native Windows tests, Linux full suite on glitch, cargo-deny, and true-TUI QA for providers, `/vault`, `/tasknode`, `/spawn`, wallet/GPU (no paid spend). Use #94's retained-behaviour checklist as the acceptance list.
6. **Afterwards:** smaller regular syncs (e.g. each upstream minor or monthly) so the gap doesn't grow back to thousands of commits.

## Recommendation (for Travis; not a decision)

Do the sync, targeting **`rust-v0.165.0`**. Start soon as a dedicated, owned program rather than in the background, because the conflict count grows weekly. If there isn't capacity for a 3–5 week program with a security review now, it's better to defer it explicitly and plan a regular cadence than to leave a half-done branch.

Measured by sync-scope94 on 2026-10-29. Raw data (conflict list, per-file hunks, merge log) is kept locally under `.codex-work/sync-scope94-data/`.

issue.title: Upstream sync: main merge #4 part B (main 465255c230..66da17e93c: #2256 Windows deny-write pinning, #2262, #2257)

repository.name: CorbanuTerminal
repository.description: Corbanu Terminal: a capital-markets-focused AI coding and agent terminal.

issue.body:
Main merge #4, part B: brings `main` `465255c230..66da17e93c` into the sync branch. It is stacked on part A (#2281); until #2281 merges, the diff also shows part A.

| main PR | What |
|---|---|
| #2256 (#1953, incl. `ebfe75c8db`, `30c5bb7168`) | Windows elevated setup creates and pins deny-write folders through no-reparse handles and applies the deny ACE to the pinned handle, so a junction a sandboxed command planted can't redirect it; policy deny paths are resolved before setup; sandbox probes isolated |
| #2262 | Management handoff docs (Nov 15) |
| #2257 (#2088) | Capability discovery and skill reads keep the D491/D510 refusal under protected levels, even with a full-disk profile; startup notice for a remote environment without its sandbox; the executor rechecks that the elevated sandbox is set up |

## How it was carried onto upstream's code
- **#1953 in `setup_provisioning.rs`** (upstream moved `bin/setup_main/win.rs` into the library): the deny-write loop now calls `deny_write_path::pin` and `add_deny_write_ace_to_handle` on the pinned handle, replacing `create_dir_all` + the path-based ACE. `deny_write_path.rs` and its tests moved to `src/setup_provisioning/` (upstream's module layout), `codex_windows_sandbox::` → `crate::`. The new #1953 step in `windows-security-probes.yml` runs those tests through `--lib` (the code is no longer in the setup binary). This closes the S3b note that the sync branch was missing #1953.
- **#2088 discovery** (`session/mcp.rs`): sandbox contexts are kept for V1 discovery under every protected level, each marked with the environment's refusal (live level; Windows level per environment, MXC as none per D522 (a)). Also applied to upstream's V2 discovery (remote executors only): under a protected level, an executor whose sandbox verdict isn't Confined is skipped and the request carries the refusal.
- **#2088 executor side** (`exec-server/src/environment.rs`): in upstream's recovering discovery closure, a root carrying a refusal is refused before any root is sent unless the executor's verdict is Confined. `local_file_system.rs` rechecks elevated setup on upstream's `windows_sandbox_selection`.
- **Startup notice** (`session/session.rs`): after upstream's environment snapshot.
- **skills.read** (`ext/skills`): kept the sync side. Upstream's skills.read no longer uses catalog-captured sandbox contexts; executor reads go through the call's live environment file system, whose context already carries the refusal.
- **D543 (a)** (recorded): `security/windows_unsandboxed_tests.rs`'s new test uses upstream's discovery signature and `windows_sandbox_selection`. `core/src/security` otherwise equals `main@66da17e93c` (the per-file delta is unchanged from part A).

## Evidence
- glitch, Rust 1.99.1: `cargo check -p codex-core -p codex-exec-server -p codex-skills-extension -p codex-windows-sandbox --lib`: 0 errors, no new warnings.
- `cargo test -p codex-exec-server --lib -- issue_2088 issue_1976 issue_2050`: 6 passed. Fail-before: with the sync tip's `environment.rs`, `issue_2088_discovery_refuses_before_sending_roots_to_an_unconfined_executor` fails.
- Windows-only code (setup_provisioning, deny_write_path, acl) is built and tested only by the Windows CI jobs. codex-core tests don't build on the branch yet, so its new tests were not built here.

## Ledger
29 `main-merge-4` rows in `ledger-rust-v0.167.0-main-merges-2.tsv` (all resolved), plus part A's review notes on its open follow-up row.

## Expected-red checks
**Expected-red checks on ef6ceaed737aa1d152f6495468c4e14d9445984d (all checks completed):**
- repo-checks / build-test: fmt-check fails only on "Rust" (rustfmt can't parse the files that still have conflict markers); the release-notes self-test errors in the log are expected negative cases. [log](https://github.com/CorbanuCore/CorbanuTerminal/actions/runs/43703889594/job/132780700885)
- CI required: red only because repo-checks is red (`check_ci_results.py`: `repo-checks: failure`). [log](https://github.com/CorbanuCore/CorbanuTerminal/actions/runs/43703889594/job/132781662313)
- Build and package, and the credential boundary canaries (Linux/macOS/Windows, push and pull_request): each fails compiling `codex-external-agent-migration` (2 errors), a crate this PR doesn't touch; the same failure is on the sync tip's own PRs (e.g. #2275's canaries). [1](https://github.com/CorbanuCore/CorbanuTerminal/actions/runs/43703885052/job/132780685777), [2](https://github.com/CorbanuCore/CorbanuTerminal/actions/runs/43703889595/job/132780699959), [3](https://github.com/CorbanuCore/CorbanuTerminal/actions/runs/43703889595/job/132780699972), [4](https://github.com/CorbanuCore/CorbanuTerminal/actions/runs/43703889595/job/132780699746)
- windows-integration-tests codex-app-server / codex-core: `codex-external-agent-migration` (same as above) and the known `RolloutItem::SourceOrigin` E0004 (#2260, fixed by #2265). [1](https://github.com/CorbanuCore/CorbanuTerminal/actions/runs/43703889593/job/132780831030), [2](https://github.com/CorbanuCore/CorbanuTerminal/actions/runs/43703889593/job/132780830992)
- rust-ci changed crate tests (macOS) codex-exec-server: the same 10 failing tests by name as main merge #3b (#2232): 3 `process_sandbox::tests::native_request_handles_remote_proxy_config_for_platform::*` and 7 `exec_process` (`codex_home_symlink_opt_out_respects_host_config_and_scope`, 6 `shell_snapshot_v2_remote_managed_proxy_uses_prepared_execution_context::*`). [log](https://github.com/CorbanuCore/CorbanuTerminal/actions/runs/43703889638/job/132780823871)
- rust-ci changed crate tests (macOS) codex-sandboxing: the same 2 failing tests as #2232 (`seatbelt::tests::create_seatbelt_args_for_cwd_as_git_repo`, `create_seatbelt_args_with_read_only_git_and_codex_subpaths`). [log](https://github.com/CorbanuCore/CorbanuTerminal/actions/runs/43703889638/job/132780823864)

The new #1953 step (`Deny-write paths never follow links`) passed: `test result: ok. 5 passed`. [log](https://github.com/CorbanuCore/CorbanuTerminal/actions/runs/43703889587/job/132780754776)

issue.title: Sync compile 6a: codex-core lib tests compile; 65 of #2296's failures fixed (security-owned paths)

repository.name: CorbanuTerminal
repository.description: Corbanu Terminal: a capital-markets-focused AI coding and agent terminal.

issue.body:
Part of #1532 / #1628, compile pass (PF-85-S02/S04). Works through #2296, security-relevant failures first.

**Result** (glitch, Rust 1.99.1, the sync tip plus this PR, `RUST_MIN_STACK` 32 MiB, the three #2294 stack-overflow tests skipped):

| | Passed | Failed |
|---|---|---|
| #2296 baseline (sync-compile4) | 4550 | 139 |
| This PR | 4619 | 80 |

- 65 of the earlier failures now pass; no new failures.
- The two test files main merge #4 brought in, plus a third that came with it, compile and pass.
- `cargo check -p codex-core --lib --profile test` has 0 errors on Linux. The Windows-only files (#2302) are not covered by this run.
- `cargo test -p codex-shell-command`: 204 passed.
- Clippy on codex-core still stops at 27 errors in the sync base's lib code. None are in files this PR touches.

**Security-relevant changes**
- **PF-23-S03 spawn (`agent/control/spawn.rs`):** S2c's port spawned through the parent's own control when the calling handle's tree lacked the parent's security binding. The child then joined the parent's tree, so the calling handle couldn't resolve, reload or wait on it. That caused about 45 failures: "live agent path not found", `ThreadNotFound`, and "no eligible child agents".
  - This PR carries main's `control_with_live_parent_security_policy`: for this spawn, the handle borrows the parent's policy view, trusted controller and session ID, and the child stays in the handle's tree.
  - A parent with no binding anywhere is still refused.
- **PF-30-S04 (`memory_stage_one_tests.rs`):** a test-fixture fix. Upstream sessions read policy through `services.security_policy`, which session construction takes from the agent control. The test replaced only `agent_control`, so the child kept reading its own policy. The fixture now joins the child to the parent's control plane the way construction does. The assertion is unchanged and passes: stage-one memory is refused under the inherited Moderate level.
- **D48 known tools (`user_namespaces_known_tool.rs`, `shell-command/src/bash.rs`):** upstream's plain-command parse refuses a script if any word could still expand (`*`, `{}`, `~`, `#`, `\`), so `nix build .#hello` was no longer offered.
  - A new `parse_shell_script_into_words_with_literal_flags` keeps main's parse and marks each word literal or not.
  - `known_tool` requires the program, the wrappers and their options to be literal; the tool's own arguments may expand.
  - `$`, backquotes, `$(...)`, subshells and redirections still refuse the script.
  - Every existing caller of the strict parse is unchanged.
- **PF-23-S01 / D334 (`protected_surface.rs`):** upstream's new built-in `send_message_to_user_async` was unclassified. It shows the person a message without ending the turn, like the model's own reply, so it is listed as having no protected effect.
- **sec-444 (`exec_policy_tests.rs`):** upstream retired UnlessTrusted's known-safe list (#39630). The safe remainder of a chain (`cat .env`) now asks, with an amendment for that remainder only. The expectation follows that stricter result; the main case (`rm notes.txt` still asks) is unchanged.
- **#2088 (`windows_unsandboxed_tests.rs`):** a remote executor with a Windows path and no configured level now gets the restricted token (upstream's `executor_windows_sandbox_level`; main forwarded Disabled). The expected selection is updated to that stricter result; the refusal assertions are unchanged.

**Other**
- **Test hook (`thread_manager.rs`, `agent/control.rs`, `cfg(test)` only):** upstream hands agent input to a thread through `start_or_steer_turn`, which `captured_ops` can't see. `captured_user_inputs` records those items so #2222's tests can check the delivered bytes, as main's checked `Op::UserInput`. `captured_ops` is unchanged.
- **`thread_manager` resume tests:** these failed after #2289's port. Upstream's legacy rollout resume reads only legacy-history threads, so the tests now start their threads with `ThreadHistoryMode::Legacy`, as upstream's own tests do.
- **#2314:** the four `shell_snapshot` credential-broker tests fail because Corbanu's hardening withholds `network.credential_providers` (#2269, decision 10). One of them shows a raw alias of `GH_TOKEN` left in the snapshot file; main has the same gap. They stay failing, not skipped.
- **Ledger:** 13 rows in `ledger-rust-v0.167.0-compile.tsv`.

No assertion was loosened. The three expectations that changed (sec-444, #2088, and the D48 parse) each follow a stricter upstream behaviour or restore main's, and each has a ledger row.

issue.title: Sync: codex-core lib tests — 4550 pass, 139 fail on the first full run (per-module list)

repository.name: CorbanuTerminal
repository.description: Corbanu Terminal: a capital-markets-focused AI coding and agent terminal.

issue.body:
This is the first full run of codex-core's lib and unit tests on the upstream-sync branch (#1532). Compile pass sync-compile4, run on glitch: Rust 1.99.1, debug build, `CORBANU_TEST_NO_NATIVE_KEYRING=1`, `RUST_MIN_STACK=32 MiB`, `--test-threads=16`.

The tree was the sync tip after #2289, plus #2290, #2291 and the PF-83 steering-test ports. Main merge #4's two new test files (`session/approval_options_tests.rs` and `tools/handlers/multi_agents_media_tests.rs`) don't compile yet; sync-main4's parts B/C cover them, so they were left out of this run. The three stack-overflow tests in #2294 were skipped.

**Result: 4550 passed, 139 failed, 10 ignored, 6 skipped (#2294).** 149 of the 174 modules pass completely.

Failing modules (passed / failed):

| tools::handlers | 267 | 51 |

| exec_policy | 110 | 1 |
| config::catalogue_effort_tests | 1 | 1 |

These looked flaky between two runs, failing in only one of them: `mcp_tool_call::tests::strict_auto_review_forces_guardian_for_mcp_policy_skip` (a tracing span error), `security::protected_additional::tests::issue_513_orchestrator_lets_only_a_person_asked_now_open_a_persistence_file`, `tools::approvals::tests::sec_513_fresh_human_authority_and_remembered_answers`, and `session::tests::task_finish_emits_thread_idle_lifecycle_after_active_turn_clears`.

Main clusters, not yet triaged:
- **About 40 `tools::handlers::multi_agents` tests and ~10 `agent::control` tests:** MultiAgentV2 path resolution fails with `live agent path '/root/worker' not found`; v2 reload returns `ThreadNotFound`; `wait_agent` reports "no eligible child agents".
- **`agent::role` project rules and project roles (D525/#2052):** hooks aren't listed, `unknown agent_type 'relay'`, and the provider allowlist and feature defaults are wrong.
- **`thread_manager` resume tests:** `thread-store unsupported operation: paginated_threads` through `resume_legacy_thread_from_rollout`. #2289 ported main's `resume_thread_from_rollout` to this function, so the port itself may be the cause.
- **Security-relevant, to check first:**
  - `memory_stage_one::...::pf_30_s04_inherited_policy_is_not_weakened_by_permissive_worker_configuration`
  - four `shell_snapshot` credential tests
  - `security::protected_surface` classification tests
  - `exec_policy::...::sec_444_remembered_prefix_does_not_cover_a_chained_command`
  - `security::user_namespaces::...::d48_known_tools_are_resolved`
- **Other areas:** world-state and rollout reconstruction (instruction updates), `code_mode_host` gRPC host tests, guardian request-layout snapshots, `spec_plan` tool exposure (`apply_patch`, `clock__sleep`), and config.

Some failures may come from the compile-pass ports in #2289/#2290/#2291, not from the sync code. Each one needs a look before it is called a product regression. Steering ports: all 14 run so far pass.
